correctness.rationale: For n=3k (k>=2), perfect matchings in a crown graph are derangements; legal alternating four-cycle switches swap two positions without creating fixed points. With target tau=sigma^{-1}, relative permutation pi^{-1}tau changes by a transposition; its cycle count must increase from k to 3k, so length =2k+2m where m is number of cycle mergers. First use of an untouched forward 3-cycle must swap with a different block (every internal swap makes a fixed point), hence first interaction merges two distinct relative cycles; each merger can first touch at most two untouched blocks, proving m>=ceil(k/2). The explicit 6-move template on two 3-blocks and 10-move template on three blocks, then disjoint-block assembly, attain equality: distance 3k (even k), 3k+1 (odd k); k=1 is disconnected. Independently applied the given templates to all k=2..20 and checked no fixed points at any step, endpoints and move count, while the universal lower bound is structural and not merely computational.
